news.title: The Elite Series heads from Hamburg to Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon
news.summary: The official 2026/27 schedule opens in Hamburg on 30–31 October, followed by London, Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon. Elite 15 and Challenger 15 races share the stage on the road to Hong Kong 2027.
news.take: Elite racing is useful when it gives everyday athletes something practical to bring back to the gym floor.

news.title: Singapore, Melbourne and Hong Kong offer an overseas start line
news.summary: The official calendar lists Singapore on 26–29 November, Melbourne on 9–13 December and Hong Kong on 7–10 January. An away race also means planning travel, sleep and recovery.
news.take: Pick a start line the crew can prepare for properly. Leave enough room around it to enjoy the achievement.

news.title: Stockholm: Australia defends its mixed-relay world title
news.summary: PUMA's World Championships report records Australia's mixed-relay win in 50:19, with Jess Pettrow on the title-defending team. Joanna Wietrzyk also finished second in the women's Elite 15 solo race.
news.take: A relay result belongs to the whole team. Agree the roles and help each other arrive prepared.

news.title: Elite qualification switches to a rolling points system
news.summary: HYROX's new framework uses a rolling 365-day window: the best five singles results or best three doubles results count. Elite Series doubles partners must share the same nationality and an active athlete licence is required.
news.take: A season is more than a list of entries. Choose the races that support the work you can sustain.

news.title: Hong Kong to host the 2027 World Championships
news.summary: HYROX announced the first World Championships in the Asia-Pacific region, at Hong Kong's AsiaWorld-Expo on 10–13 June 2027. Qualification gives the season a clear international destination.
news.take: Big targets are earned through the smaller weeks. Keep showing up with quality and intent.

news.title: Project Podium opens a new route to athlete support
news.summary: PUMA announced a programme offering men's, women's and adaptive solo podium finishers at the 2026 World Championships the opportunity to become PUMA athletes for the following season, with kit, resources and performance support.
news.take: It is encouraging to see more athletes recognised. Keep the focus on progress and the people doing the work.

races.note: Dates checked against official HYROX event listings. Travel notes are planning guidance, not live quotes or claims that the coach will attend. Refresh within 14 days before each new build.

cities.name: Dublin
cities.tagline: A short hop can still deserve a proper race-weekend plan.
gettingThere: Check the official RDS event information and your division start time before booking travel.
Compare flight, ferry and local transport against the venue journey, including luggage and registration time.

hotels.picks: Balance a practical journey to the RDS with food, sleep and somewhere easy for the crew to meet.
hotels.range: Check live rates and flexible booking terms.

food: Keep race-morning food familiar and check early breakfast options near your stay.
nightAfter: Plan a relaxed post-race meal and leave recovery time before the journey home.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.tagline: Make an overseas race a shared weekend, not a rushed turnaround.
gettingThere: Check passport, entry and airline baggage requirements before paying for travel.
Allow time to adjust to the local time zone and plan the venue journey from your chosen accommodation.

hotels.picks: Choose a base with straightforward early transport, familiar food nearby and somewhere to recover after the finish.
hotels.range: Compare live prices and flexible booking terms.

food: Keep race-morning food familiar; leave the food adventure for after the finish.
nightAfter: Plan a crew meal with enough recovery time before the flight home.

cities.name: London
cities.tagline: Choose the race slot first, then make the capital work around it.
gettingThere: This listing links to the London ExCeL event. Check the organiser's final venue instructions.
Compare your arrival station or airport with the venue journey, including weekend service changes.

hotels.picks: Prioritise a straightforward early journey over a small saving on a room across the city. Check breakfast and bag storage around your wave.
hotels.range: Hotel rates vary by date; check live prices.

food: Book a familiar meal near your hotel and carry the race fuel you have already practised with.
nightAfter: Pick a post-race meeting point before the venue gets busy.

cities.name: Melbourne
cities.tagline: A longer-haul target deserves room for travel and recovery.
gettingThere: Check the official venue and your race day before choosing flights and accommodation.
For long-haul travel, build in arrival, recovery and local time-zone adjustment rather than landing straight into a race.

hotels.picks: Compare a venue-area stay with a base near reliable public transport. Ask about early breakfast and late checkout.
hotels.range: Check live accommodation and flight prices.

food: Arrange familiar race-morning food before exploring the local options afterwards.
nightAfter: Keep the day after the race flexible before the journey home.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.tagline: Turn an international start line into a well-organised race trip.

race.name: AIA HYROX Hong Kong
race.sourceLabel: Official AIA HYROX Hong Kong event

gettingThere: Check entry requirements, airline baggage and official venue instructions before booking.
Compare the airport-to-hotel and hotel-to-venue journeys, allowing for your check-in and start time.

hotels.picks: Balance easy venue access with food, sleep and a relaxed meeting place for your crew.
hotels.range: Compare live rates and cancellation terms.

food: Keep the meal before racing predictable and enjoy the city after your finish.
nightAfter: Allow recovery time before sightseeing or flying home.

cities.name: Manchester
cities.tagline: A city race with an easy plan for the days around it.
gettingThere: Confirm the event's venue and transport guidance before choosing your station, parking or hotel.
Allow extra time if your route crosses the city, and include registration and warm-up in the plan.

hotels.area: Central or close to the venue
hotels.picks: Compare a central base for the crew meal with a shorter early journey to the race. Check breakfast, checkout and bag storage.
hotels.range: Check current rates for your particular race dates.

food: Choose a familiar pre-race dinner and an uncomplicated breakfast.
nightAfter: Agree where to meet and leave room for tired legs after the finish.
